name: Charlotte Square

dates.note: The Historic Environment Scotland record for the north block, LB28502, prints 'Robert Adam, 1793-1805'. The node's exemplar says the square was designed by Robert Adam in 1791 and built 1792-1820, which is the square as a whole. Both are recorded; neither is resolved.

refs.title: 1-11 (INCLUSIVE NOS) CHARLOTTE SQUARE WITH RAILINGS, LAMP STANDARDS AND BOUNDARY WALLS (LB28502)
refs.note: The north side, which is the palace front the node's exemplar names. The page prints 'Printed: 05/09/2026' in its own footer, so the URL resolved on the day it was read; it is percent-encoded because that is the form the register itself serves.

survey.prepared: Two extracts with different queries returned the Description and the Bibliography but never the designation date or category block, so neither is recorded here.

quotes.text: Robert Adam, 1793-1805. Symmetrical 3-storey basement and attic 27-bay neo-classical palace block consisting of 11 houses, 9 entered from front and 2 from ends.
quotes.page: Historic Environment Scotland listed building record LB28502, Description, opening sentences

quotes.text: Polished cream sandstone ashlar. Rock-faced basement; V-jointed rustication at ground floor with impost course where appropriate; cill course to 1st and 2nd floors (excepting pavilions); cornice and blocking course.
quotes.page: Historic Environment Scotland listed building record LB28502, Description

quotes.text: Timber sash and case 12-pane windows; some plate glass to rear.
quotes.page: Historic Environment Scotland listed building record LB28502, Description

quotes.text: Grey slates, ashlar coped skews; corniced ashlar stacks.
quotes.page: Historic Environment Scotland listed building record LB28502, Description

measurements.name: storey_count
measurements.as_printed: Symmetrical 3-storey basement and attic 27-bay neo-classical palace block
measurements.note: Three main storeys with the basement and attic named separately, which is the same section the London and Bath entries in this cluster describe.

measurements.name: bay_count
measurements.note: The north side read as one composition.

measurements.name: house_count
measurements.as_printed: consisting of 11 houses, 9 entered from front and 2 from ends
measurements.note: Eleven houses in twenty-seven bays: not every house is three bays, and two are entered from the ends, so the palace front is not a simple multiple of a standard house.

note: Tranche 3, 5 Sep 2026. A group record: Historic Environment Scotland lists the square in several records and this one covers the north side, Adam's palace block, which is what the node's exemplar describes. No rights statement was returned by either extract of the register page, so none is recorded rather than a line copied from another register.
